query: For magnetic high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could increase the coercive field? State one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention, the mechanism expected to alter coercivity, the predicted outcome relative to a matched baseline, the conditions under which the effect should hold, the prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an experiment with a clear result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Reducing the average grain size of a soft-magnetic CoFeNiAl0.2Cu0.2 high-entropy alloy (HEA) to the nanocrystalline regime (<100 nm) by severe plastic deformation will at least triple its room-temperature coercive field compared with the same alloy in a coarse-grained (~50 µm) homogenized state.
generation.material_initial_state: Arc-melted, homogenized CoFeNiAl0.2Cu0.2 HEA with equiaxed grains ~50 µm, single bcc solid solution, coercive field ≈ 50 Oe at 300 K.
generation.intervention: Apply high-pressure torsion (HPT) for ≥5 turns at ~6 GPa followed by a low-temperature anneal (e.g., 300 °C, 30 min) to relax defects without allowing grain growth.
generation.conditions: Room-temperature magnetic characterization in a quasistatic hysteresis loop (dH/dt ≤10 Oe s⁻¹) on bulk discs produced before and after HPT processing.
generation.structural_mediator: Nanocrystalline grain structure with a high density of grain boundaries and possible solute segregation at boundaries formed during HPT.
generation.mechanism: The increased grain-boundary area after nanocrystallization acts as an effective pinning network that impedes domain-wall motion, while solute segregation at boundaries locally enhances magnetocrystalline anisotropy. Together these raise the field required to reverse magnetization, increasing coercivity.
generation.predicted_outcome: Room-temperature coercive field will rise from ~50 Oe (baseline) to ≥150 Oe after HPT + low-T anneal without a significant reduction in saturation magnetization (≤10 % drop).
generation.baseline: The same alloy in the coarse-grained, homogenized condition measured under identical magnetic and geometric conditions.
generation.boundary: The effect should diminish if subsequent annealing coarsens grains above ~200 nm or if the alloy composition is altered to reduce magnetocrystalline anisotropy (e.g., by adding non-magnetic elements >5 at%).
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of coercivity gain is extrapolated from analogous nanocrystalline Fe-Co-Ni alloys; direct data for this specific HEA are lacking, and unforeseen defect annealing could offset gains.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two identical CoFeNiAl0.2Cu0.2 HEA discs. Characterize initial grain size and coercivity. Process one disc by HPT (≥5 turns, 6 GPa) followed by 300 °C anneal for 30 min; leave the other untreated. Measure grain size by TEM/XRD peak broadening and measure hysteresis loops for both discs at 300 K.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the processed sample shows (a) average grain size >200 nm OR (b) coercive field increase <20 % relative to baseline (i.e., Hc ≤60 Oe), the hypothesis is falsified.
